messages:
Maya: starting a geo failover sweep to compare synthetic harness vs replay harness under a 'drain' scenario. Goal: understand why tails blow up when traffic falls back to a secondary region.
Tom: do we have the run artifacts and the exact bench configs? need to reproduce head-to-head.
Maya: uploaded -> https://s3.redwood.ai/bench/1956664321/sweep.tar.gz (harness configs, qps scripts, raw traces).
Ricardo: quick note from run-3: kernel selection flips around seq_len ~1024 on us-west when KV miss-rate rises. snippet:
```
[12:23:45] req=... seq=1100 kernel=fast_attn lat=145ms
[12:23:45] req=... seq=1100 kernel=matmul_v2 lat=410ms  <-- fallback path
```
Shelby: also see batching differences. replay trace is bursty so batching packs to 6-8 requests; synth steady qps keeps batch sizes 1-2. current batching cfg:
```
batching:
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_delay_ms: 50
  continuous: true
```
Zhen: p95 summary: baseline (no drain) p95=120ms; drain+replay p95=270ms; drain+synth p95=160ms. p99 gaps larger. KV hit-rate per-run: replay ~0.58, synth ~0.82.
Maya: implies KV priming + arrival shape influence both kernel choice and batch sizing. propose controlled runs:
  A) identical per-request seq_len & prompt distribution across harnesses
  B) pre-prime KV to 90% hit-rate then run replay
  C) kernel-override run to isolate kernel impact
Tom: agree. Add runtime-commit sha and exact commands to artifacts for reproducibility.
Ricardo: kernel override flags available in bench agent: `--runtime-flag kernel_selection=prefer_dense` or `--runtime-flag kernel_selection=kv_friendly`.
Shelby: scheduling A/B and override runs now. each ~3h across 3 regions. will include job description and env vars.
perf-bot: sweep partial results posted: run-A synth p50=80ms p95=158ms p99=420ms KV-hit=0.81; run-A replay p50=95ms p95=265ms p99=840ms KV-hit=0.57. details -> https://ci.redwood.ai/build/1956664321
Maya: do we have profiling traces for the fallback samples? need flamegraphs for the ~400ms tails.
Ricardo: uploaded flamegraphs: artifacts/trace-run3/flame.svg. shows heavy time in attention kernel and memcpy spikes when kernel flips.
Zhen: working hypothesis: lower KV hit-rate triggers alternate kernel path with higher memcpy overhead; larger batches exacerbate memcpy and scheduling variance, inflating tails.
Maya: plan: run matrix over (KV primed/cold) x (synth/replay) x (kernel forced/default). collect p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate, batch-size histogram, kernel-choice freq. also record runtime sha.
Tom: paste exact commands here so we can reproduce and automate.
Shelby: commands used:
```
./harness/run_sweep --mode=synth --qps=500 --seq-dist=profiled.json --regions=us-west,eu-west --drain=us-west:90s
./harness/run_sweep --mode=replay --trace=prod-2026-02-01.json --regions=us-west,eu-west --drain=us-west:90s
./harness/run_sweep --mode=replay --trace=prod-2026-02-01.json --kernel-override=kv_friendly
```
Maya: perfect. Shelby, please drop a CSV summary with p50/p95/p99, KV hit, dominant kernel per run and link it back. Keep experiment runs idempotent and log runtime commit sha in artifacts.
Shelby: will upload CSV+README to s3 and ping here. ETA ~4.5h.
Maya: thanks team :thumbsup: keeping this thread for the next steps and follow-ups.
